<DESCRIPTION>NEWS RELEASE DATED MAY 5, 2011 AND FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
<TEXT>
<HTML><HEAD>
<TITLE>News Release Dated May 5, 2011 and Financial Statements</TITLE>
</HEAD>
 <BODY BGCOLOR="WHITE">


 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><A NAME="tx183921_5"></A>

<IMG SRC="g183921ex99_1pg001.jpg" ALT="LOGO"> </P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For Release: May&nbsp;5, 2011, 7:30 a.m. EDT </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>GM Reports Net Income of $3.2 Billion </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>Net income of $1.77 per share
including a net gain from special items of $0.82 per share </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>EBIT of $3.5 billion and EBIT-adjusted of $2.0
billion </I></B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><I>GM Europe achieves breakeven results on an EBIT-adjusted basis </I></B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">DETROIT &#150; General Motors Company (NYSE: GM) today announced first quarter net income attributable to common stockholders of $3.2 billion, or $1.77
per fully-diluted share, marking the company&#146;s fifth consecutive profitable quarter. Revenue increased $4.7&nbsp;billion to $36.2&nbsp;billion, compared with the first quarter of 2010. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#147;We are on plan,&#148; said Dan Akerson, chairman and CEO. &#147;GM has delivered five consecutive profitable quarters, thanks to strong customer demand for our new fuel-efficient vehicles and a
competitive cost structure that allows us to leverage our strong brands around the world and focus on driving profitable automotive growth.&#148; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Net income attributable to common stockholders includes gains of $1.6 billion and $0.3 billion respectively related to the sales of the company&#146;s ownership interest in Delphi Automotive LLP and
Ally&nbsp;Financial&nbsp;Inc. preferred stock. It also includes a $0.4&nbsp;billion goodwill impairment charge at GM Europe (GME) resulting from a change in accounting standards and charges totaling $0.1&nbsp;billion at GM&nbsp;International
Operations (GMIO) related to revised tax regulations affecting the company&#146;s India joint venture. Combined, these special items increased net income attributable to common stockholders by $1.5 billion or $0.82 per fully-diluted share.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) were $3.5 billion. EBIT adjusted to exclude special items was $2.0 billion compared with $1.7 billion
in the first quarter of 2010. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>GM Results Overview </B>(in billions except for per share amounts) </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GM North America (GMNA) reported EBIT of $2.9 billion compared with $1.2 billion in the first quarter of
2010. On an EBIT-adjusted basis, GMNA increased its earnings by $0.1 billion to $1.3&nbsp;billion compared with the first quarter of 2010. The company expects GMNA&#146;s quarterly EBIT-adjusted results to improve on average for the remainder of the
year compared with the first quarter as better pricing and improved fixed cost should more than offset commodity cost increases and unfavorable mix. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GME reported EBIT of $(0.4) billion. GME&#146;s results improved by $0.6 billion on an EBIT-adjusted basis compared with the first quarter of 2010 and it achieved a significant milestone by delivering
breakeven results on that basis. Based on current plans, GME is targeting to achieve breakeven results on an EBIT-adjusted basis before restructuring for the entire year. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GMIO reported EBIT of $0.5 billion compared with $0.9 billion in the first quarter of 2010. On an EBIT-adjusted basis, GMIO earned $0.6 billion in the first quarter, a decline of $0.3 billion compared
with the first quarter of 2010. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GM South America (GMSA) reported EBIT of $0.1&nbsp;billion, down $0.2 billion from the first quarter of 2010.
There were no adjustments in either period. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GM expects that full-year 2011 EBIT-adjusted results will show solid improvement over 2010. GM
continues to expect no material impact on full-year results from the Japan crisis. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For the quarter, automotive cash flow from operating
activities was $(0.6) billion and automotive free cash flow was $(1.9) billion. Both figures include the $2.5 billion cash impact of GM&#146;s decision, announced in October 2010, to end a wholesale advance agreement with Ally&nbsp;Financial.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">GM ended the quarter with very strong total automotive liquidity of $36.5 billion. Automotive cash and marketable securities, including
Canadian Health Care Trust restricted cash, was $30.6 billion compared with $27.6 billion at the end of the fourth quarter of 2010. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#147;GM
has great potential to deliver profitable growth around the world as the recovery continues,&#148; said Dan Ammann, senior vice president and CFO. &#147;While we&#146;re encouraged, we keenly recognize we have more opportunities to leverage
our&nbsp;scale, improve spending and investment efficiencies, and optimize our strong balance&nbsp;sheet.&#148; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>About General Motors</B>
&#150; General Motors (NYSE:GM, TSX: GMM), one of the world&#146;s largest automakers, traces its roots back to 1908. With its global headquarters in Detroit, GM employs 202,000 people in every major region of the world and does business in more
than 120 countries.&nbsp;GM and its strategic partners produce cars and trucks in 30 countries, and sell and service these vehicles through the following brands: Baojun, Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC, Daewoo, Holden, Isuzu, Jiefang, Opel,
Vauxhall, and Wuling. GM&#146;s largest national market is China, followed by the United States, Brazil, the United Kingdom, Germany, Canada, and Italy.&nbsp;GM&#146;s OnStar subsidiary is the industry leader in vehicle safety, security and
information services.&nbsp;More information on the new General Motors can be found at <U>www.gm.com</U>. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
